title: Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis
learning_outcomes: Explain the main security concern and trust boundary involved in Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis.
Choose an appropriate defensive control for Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis and state the assumptions under which it works.
Define a safe, reproducible verification step for Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis, including a relevant negative or failure case.

content.intro: This lesson belongs to Module 21: Secure Coding, Code Review, and Application Verification. It builds practical understanding of Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis with the syllabus subtopics retained below.
content.why_it_matters: Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis turns a security intention into evidence, an operational owner, and a repeatable control. Document the decision, owner, evidence, and review interval; verify both the control and its failure/recovery behavior before marking the task complete.

content_blocks.alt_text: Four-stage visual model for Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis: Receive file reference; Validate content + size; Isolate storage; Authorize retrieval.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis can be understood through this sequence: Receive file reference → Validate content + size → Isolate storage → Authorize retrieval. Start with the application asset and trust boundary, state what secure behavior should occur, and identify the evidence that would prove or disprove it.

content_blocks.title: Connect the syllabus subtopics
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum groups this lesson around: 160.1 Distinguishing symptoms from root causes; 160.2 Fixing shared vulnerable patterns; 160.3 Prioritizing remediation; 160.4 Avoiding incomplete patches; 160.5 Regression prevention; 160.6 Measuring remediation effectiveness. Treat these points as a checklist, not a list to memorize: explain the risk, identify the root cause, select a control, and define a test for that control.

items.title: Scope
items.text: Identify the asset, principal, input, state, or boundary affected. State whether the example is local, owned, or explicitly authorized.

items.title: Control
items.text: Document the decision, owner, evidence, and review interval; verify both the control and its failure/recovery behavior before marking the task complete.

items.title: Failure behavior
items.text: Include an invalid, denied, expired, malformed, repeated, or otherwise relevant boundary case. Fail safely without exposing secrets.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: Record expected versus actual behavior, a sanitized request or test result, the root cause, the chosen fix, and the regression test.

content_blocks.title: Safe reference example: Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis
content_blocks.code:
MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024
ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = {".png", ".jpg", ".pdf"}

# Also inspect content, generate a server-side filename,
# store outside the web root, and authorize downloads.
content_blocks.expected_output: Files larger than 5 MiB or with a non-allowlisted extension should be rejected by the corresponding server-side checks.
content_blocks.run_instructions: A filename extension and declared Content-Type are not proof of file type. Quarantine and isolate complex parsers and treat downloads as private by default.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Use a clean local test account and synthetic data. Reset the test fixture after recording the result; do not include credentials or private data in the course report.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake and recovery
content_blocks.text: Do not confuse an observation with proof or rely on a UI-only restriction. Document the decision, owner, evidence, and review interval; verify both the control and its failure/recovery behavior before marking the task complete. If evidence is ambiguous, reduce the test to one condition, inspect the application code/configuration, and repeat only within the permitted scope.

content_blocks.title: Execution and safety boundary
content_blocks.text: The current CodeLeaf playground is an HTML/CSS/JavaScript preview, not a secure runner for arbitrary server code. This example is a static reference unless the run instructions explicitly identify a supported local environment. Use a private local lab or a test system with written authorization; do not test unrelated public systems.

content.task: For “Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis”, write a short security note or test in a local/owned application. Identify the expected secure behavior, at least one relevant failure case, and the evidence needed to prove the control works.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the core rule for Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis in your own words.
Name the trust boundary and the server-side control or policy that applies.
Specify a repeatable test for expected behavior and a relevant denied/failure path.
Use synthetic data and redact credentials, tokens, and personal information from evidence.
hints: Start by stating the asset, input, actor, or trust boundary and the expected secure behavior.
Change one condition at a time; record expected and actual outcomes with synthetic data.
Check the linked official reference for framework-specific settings and version-dependent behavior.
content.expected_output: A concise control explanation and a sanitized test record showing expected/actual behavior, one failure case, and a regression check.
recap: Remediation and Root-Cause Analysis is a security boundary/control topic, not a standalone checklist item.
Document the decision, owner, evidence, and review interval; verify both the control and its failure/recovery behavior before marking the task complete.
Retest fixes and record sanitized evidence; use only authorized environments.
